A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeurOp-Diff, with matching methods, equations, datasets and experiments. All pages, including figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution experiments on UCMerced, AID and RSSCN7, including quantitative comparisons, continuous-scale evaluation and qualitative conditioning ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original super-resolution results and additionally reports runtime measurements, expanded continuous-scale results and numerical conditioning-ablation results.

M1.justification: The neural-operator conditioning, Galerkin attention, diffusion procedure, frozen pretrained operator and L1 training objective remain unchanged. Expanded symbol explanations and the scale-factor annotation in Figure 2 clarify the existing method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use UCMerced, AID and RSSCN7 for remote-sensing super-resolution, retaining fixed-scale comparisons and continuous-scale evaluation, including the same out-of-distribution scales of 9× and 10×. No dataset, domain or distinct task scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces EDiffSR with TCDM on AID and RSSCN7; the UCMerced comparator set is unchanged. Table 3 adds IDM to the continuous-scale comparison previously containing SRNO and NeurOp-Diff. These are targeted comparator changes within the retained benchmark suite.

E3.justification: v3 introduces per-image runtime evaluation at 30, 50 and 100 inference steps in Table 2 and extends LPIPS evaluation across continuous scales in Table 3. LPIPS was already used for the 4× comparison in v1. Existing training budgets, preprocessing, scale ranges and default 50-step inference remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same question about bicubic, EDSR and neural-operator conditioning, but new Table 5 supplies numerical PSNR/SSIM evidence beyond the existing qualitative comparison. Section 4.2.3 also adds analysis of runtime as inference-step count varies. The existing out-of-distribution scale analysis remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The reported evidence expands substantially through runtime results, quantitative conditioning ablations, and IDM/LPIPS results across continuous scales. For example, v3 reports 50-step times of 1.52 seconds for NeurOp-Diff, 1.79 for IDM and 2.16 for SR3, and EDSR-conditioning results of 27.42 PSNR/0.7602 SSIM. Table 1 replaces EDiffSR results with TCDM results on two datasets; these are different comparators, not updated scores for one method. Retained NeurOp-Diff scores and the comparison moved from v1 Table 2 to v3 Table 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14) retain their mathematical content. v3 changes coordinate notation and explains existing symbols and dimensions more explicitly, but adds no substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The first contribution narrows the novelty statement from first applying neural operators to remote-sensing SR to first integrating neural operators with diffusion for that task. The experimental contribution changes from six comparison methods to five. The central continuous-SR and reconstruction-quality claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions attribute improved texture recovery to richer neural-operator priors and retain the same interpretation of the PSNR versus perceptual-quality tradeoff and higher-scale behavior. Added runtime and ablation passages report supporting outcomes without introducing a different mechanism explanation, applicability boundary or substantive limitation.

D1.justification: Figure 2(b) newly makes explicit that the existing scale factor enters the lifting function, providing a limited architectural clarification. The encoder choice, pretraining schedule, optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, training iterations, GPU and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly discusses Ref-Diff and SGDM and distinguishes their fixed upscaling from continuous SR, while removing the CDGAN discussion. References also add works including RRSGAN, HSR-Diff, SSIM and LPIPS and remove EDiffSR and DCGAN. The main positioning around SR3 and SRNO remains.

P1.justification: v3 revises affiliations and contact details, clarifies method notation, edits related-work and contribution paragraphs, and adds a runtime subsection. The overall section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained, without extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Experimental presentation is substantially revised: Figure 3 replaces separate enlarged-detail rows with insets; Figure 4 adds ground-truth references; Figure 5 rearranges reference/LR columns and adds highlighted detail regions. Table 3 changes from paired-value rows to separate metric rows, two tables are added, and the former Table 2 is relocated as Table 4 with corrected PSNR highlighting. Figure 2 also gains scale-factor annotations.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens the paper by quantifying the previously qualitative conditioning ablation, adding a diffusion comparator and perceptual scores across scales, and reporting runtime evidence. Clearer notation and ground-truth references improve scrutiny. These gains are tempered by removal of the EDiffSR comparison, sparsely specified timing conditions, and smaller detail views in Figure 3. The method and retained performance results remain unchanged.
